summary: Two range lights on the Delaware River, lit April 1880 to guide ships past Cherry Island Flats; the rear tower came down in 1970-71.

structures.note: USLHS gives 13 ft; LighthouseFriends describes a 21 ft white tower. Site now a DuPont plant.
Torn down 1970-71; a skeletal tower with a red light remains nearby.

access.note: USLHS: not open to the public. LighthouseFriends: owned by the Coast Guard, grounds open, tower closed.

facts.agency: U.S. Coast Guard (rear light, per LighthouseFriends)

events.note: Range lights built: front on the Edgemoor depot pier, rear on a rise 1,456 yards north
Front light fifth-order Fresnel; rear original optic a reflector (USLHS)
Front light keeper's dwelling destroyed by fire in August; rebuilt
Rear keeper John A. Patterson injured going through a boardwalk near Shellpot Park, Wilmington
Edgemoor Depot warehouse by the front light burned
Rear range discontinued (USLHS); LighthouseFriends says tower torn down 1970 or 1971
Rear tower torn down by the Coast Guard

corrections.why: LighthouseFriends: the rear tower was torn down in 1970 or 1971; only a 1897 oil house and a skeletal tower with a red light remain. The USLHS rear record says 'Existing: Yes', which is a conflict.
LighthouseFriends: the front site is now a DuPont plant; a modern range light stands on a skeleton tower near its pier.

corrections.current: order 5 Fresnel (attached to the range station)
corrections.why: The USLHS front record gives a fifth-order Fresnel; the rear record gives a reflector as the original optic.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Two dates because two lights: the front was discontinued in 1949 (USLHS front record) and the rear in 1971 (USLHS rear record). LighthouseFriends says the rear tower came down in 1970 or 1971. The record's 1970 comes from Wikidata.

All sources agree on 1880. The Wilmington Daily Gazette of 3 April 1880 reports range lights for the channel west of Cherry Island Flats lit on the night of 1 April; LighthouseFriends and the USLHS record give 1880.

notes_for_editor: Sources: the Light-House Board's 1880 and 1878 annual reports are not in the local corpus; the 1878 appropriation and the 1880 lighting rely on LighthouseFriends and the Wilmington Daily Gazette of 3 April 1880, which names the range lights for the channel west of Cherry Island Flats without naming the range itself. The front light height conflicts: USLHS 13 ft (4.0 m) against LighthouseFriends' 21 ft tower. The rear tower is described by LighthouseFriends as a square tower on the keeper's dwelling; USLHS gives Steel and 40 ft. The rear light's status conflicts: USLHS 'Existing: Yes', LighthouseFriends says the tower was torn down. Access conflicts: USLHS says not open to the public; LighthouseFriends says Coast Guard-owned, grounds open, tower closed. Emma J. Holland (1915-1916): on the USLHS and LighthouseFriends lists only; the Wilmington newspaper search for her name turned up nothing about her service. The 1953 Wilmington Sunday Star article is known only as LighthouseFriends describes it; it was not read. Fact-check 2026-10-28: LighthouseFriends prints the 1958 keeper as Emil J. Herzog, Jr.; the USLHS line has no Jr. The 1896-97 repairs are one Board entry (no. 461, scan p.339) whose report year the volume does not fix, so the story says "By 1897". The 1899 kitchen addition is the rear entry no. 494 (scan p.132). The 1891 fire entry is no. 376 (scan p.431) and the 1891 well is no. 349 (scan p.106), both in the 1891-92 volume. The Life-Saving Service and Coast Guard keeper lists were not checked against NARA beyond the USLHS roster. Scan page numbers are the Internet Archive scan numbers (the printed page was not confirmed); the Gazette and Every Evening pages were read with the newspaper tool. Roster person slugs come from roster.py --json and are attached to each line because each line is that archive record's stint. The 1891-1892 'fiscal' labels follow the corpus volume labels, not the report title.
